A federal jury in California ordered Apple
on Friday to pay more than $5.7B in damages to Taction Technology for violating patents related to the latter's haptics technology.

At the heart of the case are two patents that Apple's Taptic Engine was accused of violating, U.S. Patent Nos. 10,659,885 and 10,820,117. Haptics are vibrations that are made by an iPhone or Apple Watch during screen touches, typing, and toggling.

The case was initially filed in 2021. Although a judge granted summary judgment in favor of Apple in 2023, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit revived the case in 2025, finding that the lower court excluded parts of Taction’s expert testimony and erred in its interpretation of the patent claims.

"Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology, which Taction’s own testing of Apple’s products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction’s technology, and we will appeal," a company spokesperson told CNBC.

title: Apple owes Taction Technology $5.7B for violating haptics patents
